claims.text: Real-time high-energy X-ray or neutron imaging during W–Cu spark-plasma sintering can enable active feedback control of temperature, pressure, and dwell time.
Imaging-guided feedback during SPS will produce a near-fully dense W–Cu composite.
Imaging-guided feedback during SPS will produce uniformly bonded W–Cu interfaces.
The imaging-guided W–Cu composite will have greater mechanical durability under fusion-relevant irradiation than W–Cu made by conventional SPS without in-situ monitoring.
Dynamic adjustment of SPS parameters based on imaging will minimize void formation.
SPS consolidation of the proposed W–Cu material will be performed at approximately 1200–1500 °C.
The proposed SPS process will be performed under vacuum or an inert atmosphere.
Real-time monitoring of densification and microstructure evolution will ensure minimal porosity.
Real-time monitoring and feedback will ensure strong W–Cu interfaces.
Closed-loop SPS adjustments will overcome processing mismatch associated with tungsten's high melting point and copper's lower boiling point.
Closed-loop SPS adjustments will prevent partial copper vaporization and binding failures.
Closed-loop SPS adjustments will promote continuous copper infiltration into the tungsten matrix.
The proposed process will reduce residual porosity to below 2% by volume.
The proposed process will improve mechanical strength relative to conventional SPS or infiltration without in-situ feedback.
The resulting composite will preserve heat-transfer capability under fusion-reactor irradiation.
SPS can provide rapid heating, short processing times, controllable microstructures, and low-porosity consolidated materials.
Implementation requires specialized X-ray or neutron beamline access and integration with SPS hardware.
Scalability and long-term irradiation behavior remain uncertain.
The magnitudes of improvements in density, thermal conductivity, and mechanical strength have not yet been quantified under fusion-relevant conditions.
Failure to observe significant improvements in porosity, mechanical properties, or thermal properties versus the unmonitored SPS control would falsify the hypothesis.
